papers.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
papers.problem: Split language models send hidden data to a server, and teams cannot compare privacy tests because attackers differ.
papers.fix: A new test framework records attacker access, and extra training gradients raised exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Attacker access changes results a lot, so a privacy claim must name its attacker.
papers.limitation: The headline test used one small model, GPT-2, in a controlled setup.

papers.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
papers.problem: Repeatedly running big AI benchmarks costs too much, and nobody knew if AI agents could build cheaper tests themselves.
papers.fix: The best agent-built tests ranked about 75% of model pairs like the real benchmarks, below the 91% ceiling.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you need a cheap test, a human-picked sample of public tasks still works well, so start there.
papers.limitation: Agent-built tests can cut off answers, run out of budget, or let a few questions dominate a score.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
papers.problem: Diffusion language models spend very different effort on outputs of the same length, and nobody knew why.
papers.fix: Story writing took over three times the passes per token of grammar fixing, and wrong math answers took more passes.
papers.practicalUseCase: Slow decoding hints at a wrong answer, so weigh answers by decoding speed when you pick one.
papers.limitation: The study covers two diffusion models across 10 tasks.

papers.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
papers.problem: Shrinking diffusion language models loses accuracy because each task and each denoising step needs a different precision.
papers.fix: T2Quant spends the bit budget by task and step, and raised accuracy by up to 6.7 percentage points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you must compress these models, give precision by step instead of one fixed setting, and you keep more accuracy.
papers.limitation: Results come from three models and six benchmarks, so other models may behave differently.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew what drives the size of sustainability sukuk issues, even as the market grew.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, longer debt, and USD or Euro gave larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you study this market, expect growth mostly in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, so look beyond them for gaps.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked clear evidence on whether AI and big data help them compete and last.
papers.fix: Among 214 surveyed staff, AI use, big data skills, and data practices all link to better competitiveness and sustainability.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run a bank, invest in AI and data tools, because staff digital skill alone did not help sustainability.
papers.limitation: The survey covers one country at one time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear what drives bank growth in countries that run both Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, ICT adoption was the strongest growth driver.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you pick where to build, digital infrastructure matters most, and high-tech exports help only when combined with ICT.
papers.limitation: The study covers 12 countries and shows statistical links, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim countries stay outside formal finance, even as Islamic finance grew for ten years.
papers.fix: In 35 OIC and OECD countries, income, tertiary education, institutional quality, and internet access drive inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you want more people banked in OIC countries, invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women, and incomes.
papers.limitation: The data covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks form sustainability committees, but nobody knew if they change environmental results in dual banking systems.
papers.fix: Committees improve all four environmental measures at conventional banks, but at Islamic banks only the overall and resource scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: When you judge an Islamic bank, check its green products, because its committee may only change the headline score.
papers.limitation: The study shows statistical links in emerging markets, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant high-stakes tests and peer comparison, and nobody knew how common impostor feelings are.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud in a tough field, know it is common, not proof.
papers.limitation: Results varied a lot between studies, by sampling method and by region, so pooled numbers need caution.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI very unevenly, and it was unclear what drives their new ideas.
papers.fix: Intrinsic and external motivation both drive innovation, and strong AI literacy makes motivation turn into new ideas more efficiently.
papers.practicalUseCase: To get more original work, build AI skill and keep motivation up, because good resources only partly cover low motivation.
papers.limitation: The data is one self-reported survey from chemistry students, so it cannot prove cause.
